newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sick pay protests disrupt Mercedes car production.
newsitem.headline: Sick pay protests disrupt Mercedes car production.

text.p: Protests against Daimler-Benz's plans to cut sick pay benefits disrupted the production of around 1,000 Mercedes-Benz cars at its plant in Bremen, the factory's works council said on Friday.
Udo Richter, head of the Bremen works council, said that in light of the current mood of the employees, he expected that workers would not show up for scheduled extra shifts on Saturday.
The Bremen works, which produces Mercedes C-class and SLK models, employes about 13,500 workers. Cancelling of the Saturday shift would disrupt production of around 300 cars.
The works council said so far only production of the C-class had been hurt and that the hot-selling SLK had not felt much impact from the protests.
Mercedes is the car and truck unit of Daimler-Benz.
According to an information booklet handed out on Friday, the works council would hold a meeting on October 8 to discuss how to further carry the fight against the sick pay cuts.
Daimler-Benz on Tuesday announced that it would take advantage of a controversial new law to cut sick pay benefits to 80 percent of gross pay, down from the normal 100 percent.
Union leaders and some political figures have protested Daimler and other companies' decisions to cut sick pay, saying the legislation applies only to future contracts and not existing ones.
